subject: Prompt set collection & next steps — model fit for Acme
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt set collection & next steps — model fit for Acme

Hi Sarah — great to meet today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary use case: customer support triage + brief syntheses for internal agents (~200 tokens avg).
- Volume: ~1.2M monthly messages, peak bursts at 10k/min.
- Quality needs: high factuality on product details, strict PII redaction for customer identifiers.

Recommended next steps from our side:
1) Share a representative prompt set (customer examples + edge cases) so we can run model-fit evals and surface regressions. Ideally: 200-500 prompts, annotated where possible.
2) Provide your redaction guidance (what counts as PII, replacement/pseudonymization rules).
3) Approve us to run a short eval (3 models, 500 prompt sample) and share the benchmark link.

Initial model recommendations (based on today):
- Redwood-optimized Llama2-70B (quantized) — good balance of accuracy/cost for long context.
- Mistral-Instruct-Large — strong few-shot instruction-following on concise syntheses.
- Small/high-throughput variant for latency-sensitive routes (we can recommend 13B quantized).

I'll run a baseline eval once we get the prompt set and redaction rules. Can you share the prompts and any internal edge cases you want covered? Attached is a simple CSV template you can use (column:prompt,expected_output,edge_case_flag).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if it's easier to walk through the prompt examples.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: prompt_template.csv (text/csv)]

From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & next steps — model fit for Acme

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the template. Attaching a CSV with ~320 prompts pulled from our support transcripts (redacted), plus our internal redaction doc (PDF). Notes below: 

- Attached files: acme_prompts.csv, acme_redaction_guidelines.pdf
- Edge cases we care about:
  * multiple-turn context where customer corrects previous info (e.g., "no, I meant plan B").
  * ambiguous product mentions (SKU vs product family).
  * sensitive PII: account numbers (10 digits), SSNs, partial credit card numbers — we want these fully redacted and replaced with [REDACTED_ACCOUNT] tokens.
  * allowable pseudonymization: first names ok to keep if consented (we'll flag those in the CSV).

Sample prompts (inlined):
1) "Customer: I can't access my account, it says account 1234567890 is locked. Agent: "
   Expected: "Ask for last login date and offer account recovery; do NOT surface the account number; redact as [REDACTED_ACCOUNT] if echoed."
2) "Customer: I need details on SKU-452 vs SKU-452-B. Agent:"
   Expected: "Clarify SKU vs variant and provide link to product page."

We can also provide an additional 200-edge-case rows if you want deeper coverage — I can get that by EOD tomorrow. We will need a short note on how Redwood handles redaction before we share anything non-redacted. Are you able to describe on your end how logs/kv cache handle prompt contents and what redaction, if any, happens server-side?

Sarah Jensen
Dir, Customer Experience — Acme Corp
sarah.jensen@acme.com
[Attachment: acme_prompts.csv (text/csv)] [Attachment: acme_redaction_guidelines.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & next steps — model fit for Acme

Hi Sarah — this is perfect, thank you. We received the CSV and the redaction guidelines. Quick answers to your questions and proposed next steps: 

- How Redwood handles prompt contents: by default, prompt inputs are processed transiently; we support optional prefix redaction and automatic KV cache eviction for sensitive routes. For Private deployments we can respect customer-managed KMS and never persist raw prompts. For Hosted API: we offer configurable PII redaction hooks and can apply a pre-ingest filter (we'll align with your rules: replace account numbers/SSNs/CC fragments with [REDACTED_ACCOUNT], etc.). Rishi can confirm the details for compliance.

- Proposed eval plan (please confirm):
  1) Run a 500-sample eval across: Redwood-llama2-70b-quant, Mistral-Instruct-Large, Redwood-13b-low-latency.
  2) Measure: factuality (precision on product details), hallucination rate, and PII leakage tests.
  3) Deliver: benchmark dashboard link + a focused regression report on flagged edge cases.

If that looks right, I'll ask Rishi to kick off the eval and Mateo to ingest the CSV and flag edge-case rows. Can you confirm whether we should treat the CSV as "redacted safe" or if you prefer we run on the copy with our pre-ingest filter?

If helpful I'll schedule a 30m post-eval walkthrough next week — what times work for you?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
https://app.redwood.com/evals/ACME-452
